scope.summary: Make oracle_db_health(invalid_objects) succeed on Oracle 18c by bounding the per-group LISTAGG sample so the 456 invalid PUBLIC synonyms on XE18 can no longer raise ORA-01489, while still reporting a run-owned invalid procedure; full DBA_OBJECTS list seen on 23ai/21c, bounded on 18c.
out_of_scope: The W4 server-level case scripts/e2e/w4/cases/ops-tools.json (w4_db_health_invalid_objects_includes_fixture_invalid_proc) is unchanged; its fixture expectation is mirrored by the live_oracle regression test instead.
No release binary / MCP-server transport run was performed here; the exercised path is the in-process run_health live path plus a direct python-oracledb probe of the generated SQL.
Other agents' in-flight edits in this shared checkout (oraclemcp-config, oraclemcp-core, oraclemcp dispatch/main, scripts/*_lint.sh) are unrelated and excluded from the claimed-path tree_clean.
Raising the server's supported minimum above 12.1 was rejected, not implemented: the fix is deliberately 12.1-portable.

entry_points.name: direct SQL probe on XE18 (planted-negative + post-fix)
entry_points.trace: python-oracledb 4.0.2 against XE18 18.0.0.0.0: the pre-fix query raised ORA-01489 code 1489 (PUBLIC/SYNONYM = 456 invalid objects, 6772 bytes of names > 4000) and the tool finding was {"attempted_views":["DBA_OBJECTS"],"error_class":"INTERNAL","ora_code":1489,"status":"failed"}. The post-fix query returns the PUBLIC/SYNONYM row with count 456 and a 400-char sample, and returns SYSTEM/PROCEDURE count 1 with SAMPLE_OBJECTS = P_BAD_RFFLX_<epoch> when the fixture exists.

limitations: LISTAGG ... ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE was implemented and validated first, then replaced before landing: it needs Oracle 12.2+, but the server supports 12.1+ (crates/oraclemcp-db/src/error.rs). The landed bounded pre-aggregation is 12.1-portable and is proven by re-execution on the 18c/21c/23ai lanes, not against a live 12.1 server.

The sample is now at most the first 20 object names per (owner, object_type) ordered by object_name, plus the outer 400-char SUBSTR cap. Previously, when a group did not overflow, the sample could carry more names up to 400 chars. The W4 expectations require the fixture group's exact single-name sample and the presence of a PUBLIC row; both are preserved.
The 20-name cap is a heuristic bound for 128-byte 12.2+ identifiers: 20*128 + 19 delimiters = 2579 < 4000. A future identifier-length increase would need the constant revisited.

Live proof ran as SYSTEM on the three local lanes, not in a scheduled CI lane, and the W4 release-binary transport case was not executed here; the in-process run_health code path it wraps is what the live_oracle test drives.

The fixture-owner assertion assumes no other invalid PROCEDURE exists for the connecting user on the lane; observed clean on all three lanes (the group reported exactly the run-owned procedure). A pre-existing invalid procedure would not break the assertion (it searches for the fixture name), only the exact-sample W4 pre23 expectation could differ.
